newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain okays new Telefonica tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Spain okays new Telefonica tariffs.

text.p: Spain's Development Ministry said on Wednesday it would approve an average interconnection charge for users of Telefonica's network of 5.1 pesetas per minute.
This would be the rate charged to Spain's planned second domestic operator Retevision for using Telefonica's network.
The ministry also approved rises in Telefonica's local call and fixed tariffs for 1998 and 1999, along with cuts in its international and long distance call rates.
Telefonica's fixed line-rental tariff will rise 100 pesetas in March 1998, and a further 100 pesetas in August of that year.
There will be four hikes in local call rates of 0.25 pesetas per minute in April, August and December 1998 and then again in March 1999.
Provincial calls will fall five percent in 1998, and by 10 percent in 1999. They will subsequently be reduced 15 percent in 1998, and by a further 20 percent in 1999.
Long distance calls will fall by 11 percent this year, by 15 percent in 1998 and by another 20 percent in 1999.
International calls fell 8.8 percent this month, and will fall a further 12 percent both in 1998 and in 1999.
For other domestic operators using Telefonica's network local charges will be 2.5 pesetas per minute both standard and peak rate, and 2.30 pesetas per minute off-peak.
Provincial charges will be 3.87 pesetas per minute standard rate, 4.25 pesetas at peak times and 2.38 pesetas off-peak.
Long-distance charges will be 4.97 pesetas per minute standard rate, 7.00 pesetas at peak times and 3.01 pesetas off-peak.

In a statement, the Development Ministry said until Telefonica's charges have been completely rebalanced, new tariff regulations specify that any operator achieving a 10 percent local market share or a 15 percent share of any other segment would be "obliged to contribute to financing the so-called access deficit that Telefonica has."
